citations.quote: Years later, agents come to me with almost the same problem, just in a different form. “I don’t know how to follow up.” “Clients disappear after Zoom.” “I send options and hear nothing.” “I don’t know how to qualify properly.” “They are speaking to five other brokers.” “Why should they choose me?”

observation.text: The text is structured to first present the problem agents face, using an enumeration of dialogue snippets that reflect common issues, followed by the realization that even with modern CRM systems, the fundamental challenge persists.

citations.quote: How to create enough interest for the next step? How to keep them engaged? How to understand what actually matters to them.

observation.text: The text uses a series of rhetorical questions to highlight challenges in engaging clients, framed as common struggles.

citations.quote: Most business came through cold calling or referrals.

summary.text: Most business came through cold calling or referrals in Dubai real estate in 2015.

citations.quote: So I learned sales by speaking to people who did NOT ask me to call them.

summary.text: The author learned sales by speaking to people who did not ask her to call them.

citations.quote: even with social media leads landing directly in your CRM, agents are still facing the same core sales problem.

summary.text: Agents face the core sales problem of leading a conversation with someone who does not yet see a reason to keep talking.

citations.quote: That is a skill. And it can be learned.

summary.text: Leading a conversation to create enough interest and keep clients engaged is a learnable skill.
